articles.title: The .pth file that runs before your code: lessons from the LiteLLM 1.107.0 compromise
articles.excerpt: The .pth file that runs before your code: lessons from the LiteLLM 1.107.0 compromise Version 1.107.0 of the LiteLLM Python package was published with a credential stealer and a backdoor inside it. Th…
articles.body: The .pth file that runs before your code: lessons from the LiteLLM 1.107.0 compromise Version 1.107.0 of the LiteLLM Python package was published with a credential stealer and a backdoor inside it. The package has been quarantined on PyPI and the malicious Docker images have been removed. The delivery mechanism is what makes this incident worth a closer reading rather than the payload list. A path configuration file executes Python before any application import, so an operator who never called a LiteLLM function could still be compromised. What happened LiteLLM's director of security said the malicious actions were taken through three engineers' GitHub accounts, apparently by way of stolen GitHub CLI OAuth tokens. One account triggered the project-releaser run and another approved it.
articles.author: yutianle

articles.body: Today, I learned about HTML meta tags and started exploring React.js. I also learned the difference between a library and a framework and how to set up a React project using the terminal. 1. What Are Meta Tags in HTML? Meta tags provide information about a webpage to browsers and search engines. They are placed inside the section of an HTML document. Example <head> <meta charset="UTF-8"> <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0"> <meta name="description" content="My web development learning journey"> <title>My Website</title> </head> charset="UTF-8" supports a wide range of characters. name="viewport" helps webpages display properly on different screen sizes.

You wrote the hook everyone writes. function useOnlineStatus () { const [ online , setOnline ] = useState ( navigator . onLine ); useEffect (() => { const update = () => setOnline ( navigator . onLine ); window . addEventListener ( ' online ' , update ); window . addEventListener ( ' offline ' , update ); return () => { window . removeEventListener ( ' online ' , update ); window . removeEventListener ( ' offline ' , update ); }; }, []); return online ; } It worked in every app you shipped before React 18.

articles.title: NestJS 12 Lifecycle Hooks: The Order You Can't Assume
articles.excerpt: A NestJS app upgrades from v11 to v12. No application code changes — just npm i @nestjs/core@latest @nestjs/common@latest. The test suite, which has been green for months, starts failing intermittentl…
articles.body: A NestJS app upgrades from v11 to v12. No application code changes — just npm i @nestjs/core@latest @nestjs/common@latest . The test suite, which has been green for months, starts failing intermittently: a report service reads a cache that a metrics service is supposed to have already populated, and about one run in three, it hasn't been. Nothing in the diff touches either service. The bug was always there — it just used to be invisible, because the old, undocumented order happened to keep working. The official v12.0.0 release notes list the cause in one line, under breaking changes: "Lifecycle hooks are now invoked by component hierarchy level." The fix isn't a workaround for v12 — it's realizing that "hook order" was never a promise Nest made for providers like these two.

articles.title: Europe's Space Rider vehicle comes crashing down during drop test
articles.excerpt: The full-scale prototype of Europe's Space Rider orbiter failed to deploy its parachute during a drop test earlier this month, but ESA officials hope the setback won't delay progress toward its first…
articles.body: Europe has dropped the ball on the prototype for its first reusable spacecraft. Or, rather, the prototype itself was dropped — on purpose — but the outcome of its fall was not what engineers had hoped for. The incident occurred during an Oct. 6 drop test of the full-scale Space Rider model , from the European Space Agency (ESA). The robotic vehicle's initial drogue parachute deployed successfully, but its main parafoil detached during deployment, leaving the prototype unable to slow its descent before crashing into the ground, according to ESA officials. The cause of the failure remains under investigation.

articles.body: NASA, ESA, Michael Jones (California Institute of Technology); Image Processing: Gladys Kober (NASA/Catholic University of America) This NASA Hubble Space Telescope image released on Oct. 16, 2026, features the edge-on, intermediate spiral galaxy NGC 1827, located roughly 37 million light-years away in the constellation Columba, the Dove. Hubble captured the image as part of a survey looking at 260 satellite galaxies around 22 Milky Way-like host galaxies within a radius of about 32 million light-years from Earth. Low-mass galaxies like the ones in this Hubble observing program provide a way to test the predictions of cosmological models on small scales, which struggle to match observations.

articles.title: On this day in space! Oct. 22, 1992: Ashes of 'Star Trek' creator Gene Roddenberry launch into space on NASA shuttle
articles.excerpt: On Oct. 22, 1992, the space shuttle Columbia launched into space with the ashes of Gene Roddenberry, the creator of "Star Trek." Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Oct. 22, 1992, the space shuttle Columbia launched into space with the ashes of Gene Roddenberry, the creator of " Star Trek ," aboard. During mission STS-52, NASA astronaut and shuttle commander James Wetherbee brought a small container with a portion of Roddenberry's ashes into space as part of his personal effects at the request of Roddenberry's widow, Majel Barrett . It was Roddenberry's lifelong dream to go to space, but he never got to go while he was alive. But thanks to his wife, a little bit of Roddenberry finally made it to space almost exactly one year after his death. NASA and his family didn't tell anyone about it until almost two years later in 1994. Wetherbee said he was "honored to be asked" by Barrett to carry Roddenberry's ashses on the spaceflight.
